subjects.name: Process Control in Spinning and Weaving
subjects.name_print: Process Control in Spinning and Weaving

units.1:
Process control and its importance, application of various tools and techniques for process control, cotton fibre selection and bale management system, ways to achieve quality and cost optimization, control of waste in spinning, cleaning efficiency of blow room and card, yarn realization, control of neps and fibre rupture, assessment of performance of blow room & card.
Total Lectures Required: 8
units.2:
Means to improve productivity and machine efficiency, controlling end-breakage rate in ring spinning, control of yarn faults and package defects, classimat faults, control of yarn quality- count, lea strength and their variability, study of CV% (within bobbin and between bobbin), single yarn strength and elongation, control of yarn unevenness, imperfections and hairiness, process control measures at different stages of yarn spinning.
Total Lectures Required: 8
units.3:
Scope of process control in weaving, systems of process control in weaving, setting norms and schedule of checks, machinery audit, optimizing quality of winding, control of quality of knot, producing good package, dressing of the beams for reducing incidence of cross ends.
Total Lectures Required: 8
units.4:
Process control in warping, minimizing end-breakage in warping, quality of warping beam, control of productivity, factors responsible for loss in efficiency, control of productivity, process control in sizing, choice of recipe and size pick-up, control of size pick-up, control of yarn stretch, quality of sized beams.
Total Lectures Required: 8
units.5:
Process control in loom shed, snap study, time and motion study, control of warp and weft breakage, causes and remedies of fabric defects, factors responsible for loss in efficiency, control of productivity, process control in grey inspection, and folding sections
Total Lectures Required: 8

cos.text: Explain the importance of process control in various area of spinning process.
Describe productivity, means to improve productivity, maximizing machine efficiency in ring spinning.
Explain process control in weaving, setting norms and schedule of checks, machinery audit.
Explain process control in warping, minimizing end breakage in warping, quality of warping beam,
Explain process control in loom shed, snap study and time and motion study, control of warp and weft breakage, causes and remedies of fabric defects.

textbooks.book: Process Control in Textile Manufacturing, edited by A, Majumdar, A. Das, R. Alagirusamy and V. K. Kothari, Woodhead Publisher (2011).
Evenness Testing in Yarn Production, Part I and II, by R. Fruter, The Textile Institute, Manchester (1982).
Seminar on Process Control in Spinning, Edited by R. Chattopadhyay, IIT Delhi (2001),
On line Quality Control in Spinning and Weaving, Textile progress, Vol 17, No.1/2
Total Quality management by D. H. Besterfield, C. Besterfield-Michna, G. H. Besterfield, M. Besterfield-Sacre, H. Urdhwareshe, R. Urdhwareshe, Pearson, New Delhi (2012).

objectives_print: To familiarize the students with concept of process control, tools and techniques of process control and its importance in achieving quality objectives and reduction of waste.
To familiarize the students on various process and quality related problems faced during yarn production and measures to achieve quality objectives.
To understand scope and systems of process control in weaving, setting norms and schedule of checks, machinery audit.
To understand the process control in warping, minimizing end breakage in warping, quality of warping beam.
To understand the process control in loom shed, snap study, time and motion study, control of warp and weft breakage, causes and remedies of fabric defects.

units.1:
Overview of Indian and Global apparel industry, Introduction to garment manufacturing
process, Garment classification; familiarisation with body measurements for men, women and
kids; patternmaking terminologies.
units.2:
Pre-Sewing Operations: principles and objectives of marker planning, marker efficiency,
computerised marker planning techniques, fabric spreading and its requirements, cutting process-
objective of cutting, different methods of cutting; fusing-means, equipment, methods, and
requirements.
units.3:
Sewing and finishing: Definition of stitch and seam, their classifications and
applications; methods of stitch formation, Classification of sewing machines, commonly used
sewing machines and their main parts and functions; Different feed systems; Sewing thread–
types, properties, applications, ticket number; Calculations of sewing thread consumption, sewing
needles and its types; garment finishing processes, Pressing- purpose, categories, means,
equipment and methods.
units.4:
Production Planning and Industrial Engg: Introduction to Industrial Engg, Concept of
SAM, SMV, Performance Rating, allowances, Productivity, Efficiency, Time study and Method
study; Line-balancing, preparation of operation bulletin, work-aids; Production Planning and
Control.
units.5:
Quality Control: Fabric inspection systems; sewing thread quality requirements; cutting
and fusing defects, stitch and seam defects, sewing defects; finishing defects, Acceptable quality
level(AQL).

cos.text: Understand human body measurements and pattern making terminologies.

Apply marker planning, spreading, cutting, sewing and finishing techniques in garment   
            industry.
Identify and explain various types of machinery used in garment manufacturing.
Apply industrial engineering concepts in garment industry.
Identify and resolve quality issues occurring at different stages of garment manufacturing.

subjects.name: High Performance Fibres and Composites

units.1: Introduction, history and development of high-performance fibres, Aramid fibres, polymerisation of meta and para-aramid, concept of liquid crystalline state, dry-jet wet spinning, structure and properties of aramids, applications, introduction about other high-performance fibre, UHMWPE, Aromatic polyester, PBO and PEEK.
units.2: Carbon fibre, Precursors for carbon fibre, Rayon based, PAN based, and pitch based carbon fibres, Stabilisation, Carbonisation and Graphitisation, Comparison of carbon fibres from precursors, Surface treatment of carbon fibre, properties and applications, Introduction to Glass fibre, Ceramic fibre, properties and applications.
units.3: Definitions, Composites, Reinforcements and matrices, Types of reinforcements, Types of matrices, Types of composites, Carbon Fibre composites, Properties of composites in comparison with standard materials, Applications of metal, ceramic and polymer matrix composites.
units.4: Hand and spray lay - up, injection molding, resin injection, filament winding, pultrusion, centrifugal casting and prepregs. Fibre/Matrix Interface, mechanical. Textile composites: Constituents of composites, roles of reinforcement, matrix and interface, different forms of reinforcement, Thermoplastic and thermoset matrices, 3D Woven Textile Structural Polymer Composites.
units.5: Design, Development, and Characterization of Advanced Textile Structural Hollow Composites, Testing of composites, tensile, bending and impact testing, three-point bending test, Izod and Charpy impact tests and their differences, Dynamic mechanical analysis, Storage and loss moduli and damping factor.

cos.text: Understand high-performance fibre, aramid fibre types, polymerisation of aramide and other high-performance fibres.
Carbon fibre precursors types, process of manufacturing carbon fibres, properties and applications, introduction of glass fibre and ceramic fibre.
Basics of composites and its types, properties and applications of carbon fibre composite, polymer fibre composites.
Different techniques to prepare prepegs, manufacturing of textile composites, 3D woven composites.
Design and development of hollow composites, testing and characterization of composite materials.

textbooks.book: High Performance Fibres, by J. W. S. Hearle, Woodhead Publishing, 2001
High Performance Fibres by S. K. Mukhopadyay, Textile progress Vol. 25, Textile Institute, Manchester, 1993
An Introduction to Composite Materials by D. Hull and T.W. Clyne, Cambridge University Press; 3rd edition, 2019
Fiber Reinforced Composites Materials: Manufacturing, and Design by P. K. Mallick, CRC Press, 2008
Analysis and Performance of Fiber Composites by B. D. Agarwal, L. J. Broutman, K. Chandrashekhara, Wiley, 2015
Composite Materials: Science and Engineering by K. K. Chawla, Springer, 2015
Advances in Textile Structural Composite by Rajesh Mishra, Polymers MDPI, 2023
NPTEL course on High Performance and Speciality Fibres by M. Jassal, IIT Delhi

objectives_print: The objective of this course is to introduce the manufacturing methods and properties of various high-performance fibres known for their high tensile properties or thermal resistance.
Another objective of this course is to familiarize the students with fibre reinforced composites, their manufacturing methods and evaluation.

subjects.name: Sustainability in Textile Industry
objectives_print: The course aims to introduce the concept of sustainability in various stages of textile and apparel manufacturing, understanding of the environmental issues in textile supply chain and familiarity with guidelines and regulations that support sustainable textile production practices.

units.1: Defining sustainability and circularity, three dimensions of sustainability, sustainable development goals, Net zero. Environmental impacts of textile and fashion industry, resource consumption (water, energy etc.) in fibre production, yarn manufacturing, fabric manufacturing, and chemical processing; Types of emissions, scopes I, II and III, measuring carbon footprints, decarbonizing textile supply chain; Case study of Tirupur textile industry.
units.2: Sustainable textile processes, restricted substances for textile and clothing industry; Concepts of green chemistry, natural dyeing, supercritical carbon dioxide, ozone, UV and plasma technologies, foam dyeing, dope dyed fibres; Renewable energy sources, solar, hydro, wind, etc. Effluent treatment, primary, secondary and tertiary treatments, zero liquid discharge (ZLD); Standards of BOD, COD, TDS, TSS, pH, and heavy metals.
units.3: Circularity, circular design, 3Rs (reduce, reuse and recycle), RESOLVE framework, restoration and regeneration; Textile recycling, upcycling, and downcycling, open-loop and close- loop recycling, sorting technology; Methods of recycling, mechanical, thermal and chemical recycling, recycling of pre and post-consumer textiles, challenges.
units.4: Life cycle analysis, cradle-to-gate, cradle-to-grave, and cradle-to-cradle approaches, cut- off and allocation approaches, system boundary; Steps of LCA, unit of analysis, inventory assessment, impact assessment, and interpretation; Case studies related to LCA analysis of textile products. Traceability- the need for traceability in the textile value chain, use of blockchain and fibre tags/coins for traceability
units.5: Standards and certifications, needs, ISO 14000, Oeko-tex 100, Higg- index, GOTS, SMETA members ethical trade audit (SEDEX), Global Recycled Standard (GRS). Environmental, social and governance (ESG) factors, social sustainability issues in textile and fashion industry, governance mechanisms; Case of Rana Plaza disaster.
